import datetime

from django.core.exceptions import ValidationError
from django.forms import ModelForm, BaseModelForm
from django.test import TestCase

from .models import Article, Author, Book, Category, Writer


class BaseModelFormValidateUniqueTests(TestCase):
    def test_validate_unique_success(self):
        """Test that validate_unique() does not raise an error when the instance is unique."""
        class TestModelForm(BaseModelForm):
            class Meta:
                model = Article
                fields = ['title']

        article = Article.objects.create(title="Test Article")
        form = TestModelForm(instance=article)
        form.clean()
        form.save()
        self.assertTrue(Article.objects.filter(title="Test Article").exists())

    def test_validate_unique_failure(self):
        """Test that validate_unique() raises a ValidationError when the instance is not unique."""
        class TestModelForm(BaseModelForm):
            class Meta:
                model = Article
                fields = ['title']

        article1 = Article.objects.create(title="Test Article")
        article2 = Article.objects.create(title="Test Article")
        form = TestModelForm(instance=article2)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            form.clean()

    def test_validate_unique_with_exclude(self):
        """Test that validate_unique() excludes specified fields."""
        class TestModelForm(BaseModelForm):
            class Meta:
                model = Article
                fields = ['title', 'pub_date']
                exclude = ['writer']

        article1 = Article.objects.create(title="Test Article", pub_date=datetime.date(2023, 1, 1))
        article2 = Article.objects.create(title="Test Article", pub_date=datetime.date(2023, 1, 1))
        form = TestModelForm(instance=article2)
        form.clean()
        self.assertTrue(Article.objects.filter(title="Test Article", pub_date=datetime.date(2023, 1, 1)).exists())

    def test_validate_unique_with_existing_instance(self):
        """Test that validate_unique() works correctly with an existing instance."""
        class TestModelForm(BaseModelForm):
            class Meta:
                model = Article
                fields = ['title']

        article = Article.objects.create(title="Original Title")
        form = TestModelForm(instance=article)
        form.clean()
        form.save()
        self.assertEqual(Article.objects.get(pk=article.pk).title, "Original Title")

    def test_validate_unique_with_new_instance(self):
        """Test that validate_unique() works correctly with a new instance."""
        class TestModelForm(BaseModelForm):
            class Meta:
                model = Article
                fields = ['title']

        form = TestModelForm(data={'title': 'New Title'})
        form.clean()
        article = form.save()
        self.assertEqual(Article.objects.get(pk=article.pk).title, "New Title")

from .models import Article, Author, Book, Category, Writer


class ModelChoiceFieldTests(TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        cls.c1 = Category.objects.create(name='Entertainment', slug='entertainment', url='entertainment')
        cls.c2 = Category.objects.create(name='A test', slug='test', url='test')
        cls.c3 = Category.objects.create(name='Third', slug='third-test', url='third')

    def test_basics(self):
        f = forms.ModelChoiceField(Category.objects.all())
        self.assertEqual(list(f.choices), [
            ('', '---------'),
            (self.c1.pk, 'Entertainment'),
            (self.c2.pk, 'A test'),
            (self.c3.pk, 'Third'),
        ])
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            f.clean('')
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            f.clean(None)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            f.clean(0)

        # Invalid types that require TypeError to be caught.
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            f.clean([['fail']])
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            f.clean([{'foo': 'bar'}])

        self.assertEqual(f.clean(self.c2.id).name, 'A test')
        self.assertEqual(f.clean(self.c3.id).name, 'Third')

        # Add a Category object *after* the ModelChoiceField has already been
        # instantiated. This proves clean() checks the database during clean()
        # rather than caching it at  instantiation time.
        c4 = Category.objects.create(name='Fourth', slug='4th', url='4th')
        self.assertEqual(f.clean(c4.id).name, 'Fourth')

        # Delete a Category object *after* the ModelChoiceField has already been
        # instantiated. This proves clean() checks the database during clean()
        # rather than caching it at instantiation time.
        Category.objects.get(url='4th').delete()
        msg = "['Select a valid choice. That choice is not one of the available choices.']"
        with self.assertRaisesMessage(ValidationError, msg):
            f.clean(c4.id)

    def test_clean_model_instance(self):
        f = forms.ModelChoiceField(Category.objects.all())
        self.assertEqual(f.clean(self.c1), self.c1)
        # An instance of incorrect model.
        msg = "['Select a valid choice. That choice is not one of the available choices.']"
        with self.assertRaisesMessage(ValidationError, msg):
            f.clean(Book.objects.create())

    def test_clean_to_field_name(self):
        f = forms.ModelChoiceField(Category.objects.all(), to_field_name='slug')
        self.assertEqual(f.clean(self.c1.slug), self.c1)
        self.assertEqual(f.clean(self.c1), self.c1)

    def test_choices(self):
        f = forms.ModelChoiceField(Category.objects.filter(pk=self.c1.id), required=False)
        self.assertIsNone(f.clean(''))
        self.assertEqual(f.clean(str(self.c1.id)).name, 'Entertainment')
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            f.clean('100')

        # len() can be called on choices.
        self.assertEqual(len(f.choices), 2)

        # queryset can be changed after the field is created.
        f.queryset = Category.objects.exclude(name='Third')
        self.assertEqual(list(f.choices), [
            ('', '---------'),
            (self.c1.pk, 'Entertainment'),
            (self.c2.pk, 'A test'),
        ])
        self.assertEqual(f.clean(self.c2.id).name, 'A test')
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            f.clean(self.c3.id)

        # Choices can be iterated repeatedly.
        gen_one = list(f.choices)
        gen_two = f.choices
        self.assertEqual(gen_one[2], (self.c2.pk, 'A test'))
        self.assertEqual(list(gen_two), [
            ('', '---------'),
            (self.c1.pk, 'Entertainment'),
            (self.c2.pk, 'A test'),
        ])

        # Overriding label_from_instance() to print custom labels.
        f.queryset = Category.objects.all()
        f.label_from_instance = lambda obj: 'category ' + str(obj)
        self.assertEqual(list(f.choices), [
            ('', '---------'),
            (self.c1.pk, 'category Entertainment'),
            (self.c2.pk, 'category A test'),
            (self.c3.pk, 'category Third'),
        ])

    def test_choices_freshness(self):
        f = forms.ModelChoiceField(Category.objects.all())
        self.assertEqual(len(f.choices), 4)
        self.assertEqual(list(f.choices), [
            ('', '---------'),
            (self.c1.pk, 'Entertainment'),
            (self.c2.pk, 'A test'),
            (self.c3.pk, 'Third'),
        ])
        c4 = Category.objects.create(name='Fourth', slug='4th', url='4th')
        self.assertEqual(len(f.choices), 5)
        self.assertEqual(list(f.choices), [
            ('', '---------'),
            (self.c1.pk, 'Entertainment'),
            (self.c2.pk, 'A test'),
            (self.c3.pk, 'Third'),
            (c4.pk, 'Fourth'),
        ])

    def test_choices_bool(self):
        f = forms.ModelChoiceField(Category.objects.all(), empty_label=None)
        self.assertIs(bool(f.choices), True)
        Category.objects.all().delete()
        self.assertIs(bool(f.choices), False)

    def test_choices_bool_empty_label(self):
        f = forms.ModelChoiceField(Category.objects.all(), empty_label='--------')
        Category.objects.all().delete()
        self.assertIs(bool(f.choices), True)

    def test_choices_radio_blank(self):
        choices = [
            (self.c1.pk, 'Entertainment'),
            (self.c2.pk, 'A test'),
            (self.c3.pk, 'Third'),
        ]
        categories = Category.objects.all()
        for widget in [forms.RadioSelect, forms.RadioSelect()]:
            for blank in [True, False]:
                with self.subTest(widget=widget, blank=blank):
                    f = forms.ModelChoiceField(
                        categories,
                        widget=widget,
                        blank=blank,
                    )
                    self.assertEqual(
                        list(f.choices),
                        [('', '---------')] + choices if blank else choices,
                    )

    def test_deepcopies_widget(self):
        class ModelChoiceForm(forms.Form):
            category = forms.ModelChoiceField(Category.objects.all())

        form1 = ModelChoiceForm()
        field1 = form1.fields['category']
        # To allow the widget to change the queryset of field1.widget.choices
        # without affecting other forms, the following must hold (#11183):
        self.assertIsNot(field1, ModelChoiceForm.base_fields['category'])
        self.assertIs(field1.widget.choices.field, field1)

    def test_result_cache_not_shared(self):
        class ModelChoiceForm(forms.Form):
            category = forms.ModelChoiceField(Category.objects.all())

        form1 = ModelChoiceForm()
        self.assertCountEqual(form1.fields['category'].queryset, [self.c1, self.c2, self.c3])
        form2 = ModelChoiceForm()
        self.assertIsNone(form2.fields['category'].queryset._result_cache)

    def test_queryset_none(self):
        class ModelChoiceForm(forms.Form):
            category = forms.ModelChoiceField(queryset=None)

            def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
                super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
                self.fields['category'].queryset = Category.objects.filter(slug__contains='test')

        form = ModelChoiceForm()
        self.assertCountEqual(form.fields['category'].queryset, [self.c2, self.c3])

    def test_num_queries(self):
        """
        Widgets that render multiple subwidgets shouldn't make more than one
        database query.
        """
        categories = Category.objects.all()

        class CategoriesForm(forms.Form):
            radio = forms.ModelChoiceField(queryset=categories, widget=forms.RadioSelect)
            checkbox = forms.ModelMultipleChoiceField(queryset=categories, widget=forms.CheckboxSelectMultiple)

        template = Template(
            '{% for widget in form.checkbox %}{{ widget }}{% endfor %}'
            '{% for widget in form.radio %}{{ widget }}{% endfor %}'
        )
        with self.assertNumQueries(1):
            template.render(Context({'form': CategoriesForm()}))

    def test_prepare_value_with_meta(self):
        class ModelChoiceForm(forms.Form):
            category = forms.ModelChoiceField(Category.objects.all(), to_field_name='slug')

        form = ModelChoiceForm()
        self.assertEqual(form.fields['category'].prepare_value(self.c1), self.c1)

    def test_prepare_value_without_meta(self):
        class ModelChoiceForm(forms.Form):
            category = forms.ModelChoiceField(Category.objects.all())

        form = ModelChoiceForm()
        self.assertEqual(form.fields['category'].prepare_value(self.c1), self.c1)

    assert _pytest.compat._idval(1.0, "arg", 0, None, None, None) == "1.0"

class MigrationPlanTests(TestCase):

        """

        executor.loader = mock.Mock()
        executor.loader.graph = MigrationGraph()
        plan = executor.migration_plan([])
        self.assertEqual(plan, [])

    def test_migration_plan_single_target_unapplied(self):
        """
        Tests that migration_plan returns the correct plan when a single
        target is unapplied.
        """
        executor = MigrationExecutor(None)
        executor.loader = mock.Mock()
        executor.loader.graph = MigrationGraph()
        executor.loader.graph.add_node(('app', 'migration'), mock.Mock())
        executor.loader.applied_migrations = {('app', 'migration') : mock.Mock()}

        plan = executor.migration_plan([('app', 'migration')])
        self.assertEqual(len(plan), 1)
        self.assertEqual(plan[0][1], False)

    def test_migration_plan_single_target_applied(self):
        """
        Tests that migration_plan returns an empty list when a single
        target is already applied.
        """
        executor = MigrationExecutor(None)
        executor.loader = mock.Mock()
        executor.loader.graph = MigrationGraph()
        executor.loader.graph.add_node(('app', 'migration'), mock.Mock())
        executor.loader.applied_migrations = {('app', 'migration') : mock.Mock()}

        plan = executor.migration_plan([('app', 'migration')])
        self.assertEqual(plan, [])

    def test_migration_plan_multiple_targets_mixed(self):
        """
        Tests that migration_plan returns the correct plan when multiple
        targets are mixed (some applied, some unapplied).
        """
        executor = MigrationExecutor(None)
        executor.loader = mock.Mock()
        executor.loader.graph = MigrationGraph()
        executor.loader.graph.add_node(('app1', 'migration1'), mock.Mock())
        executor.loader.graph.add_node(('app2', 'migration2'), mock.Mock())
        executor.loader.applied_migrations = {('app1', 'migration1') : mock.Mock()}

        plan = executor.migration_plan([('app1', 'migration1'), ('app2', 'migration2')])
        self.assertEqual(len(plan), 1)
        self.assertEqual(plan[0][0], executor.loader.graph.nodes[('app2', 'migration2')])
        self.assertEqual(plan[0][1], False)

    def test_migration_plan_clean_start(self):
        """
        Tests that migration_plan returns the correct plan when clean_start
        is True.
        """
        executor = MigrationExecutor(None)
        executor.loader = mock.Mock()

        executor.loader.applied_migrations = {('app', 'migration') : mock.Mock()}

        plan = executor.migration_plan([('app', 'migration')], clean_start=True)
        self.assertEqual(plan, [])

class TestMigrationExecutorCreateProjectState(MigrationTestBase):
    def test_create_project_state_with_applied_migrations(self):
        """
        Tests that _create_project_state correctly mutates the state
        with applied migrations.
        """
        executor = MigrationExecutor(None)
        graph = MigrationGraph()
        migration1 = migrations.Migration('app1', '0001')
        migration2 = migrations.Migration('app1', '0002')
        graph.add_node((migration1.app_label, migration1.name), migration1)
        graph.add_node((migration2.app_label, migration2.name), migration2)
        graph.add_dependency(None, (migration2.app_label, migration2.name), (migration1.app_label, migration1.name))

        executor.loader = type('FakeLoader', (object,), {
            'graph': graph,
            'applied_migrations': {(migration1.app_label, migration1.name): migration1,
                                   (migration2.app_label, migration2.name): migration2},
            'unmigrated_apps': ['app1']
        })

        state = executor._create_project_state(with_applied_migrations=True)

        self.assertEqual(len(state.models), 2)
        self.assertIn(('app1', '0001'), state.models)
        self.assertIn(('app1', '0002'), state.models)

    def test_create_project_state_without_applied_migrations(self):
        """
        Tests that _create_project_state creates a state without
        applied migrations when with_applied_migrations is False.
        """
        executor = MigrationExecutor(None)
        graph = MigrationGraph()
        migration1 = migrations.Migration('app1', '0001')
        graph.add_node((migration1.app_label, migration1.name), migration1)

        executor.loader = type('FakeLoader', (object,), {
            'graph': graph,
            'applied_migrations': {},
            'unmigrated_apps': ['app1']
        })

        state = executor._create_project_state(with_applied_migrations=False)

        self.assertEqual(len(state.models), 1)
        self.assertIn(('app1', '0001'), state.models)

        if all its replaced migrations are already applied.
        """

        recorder.record_applied("migrations", "0001_initial")
        recorder.record_applied("migrations", "0002_second")

        executor = MigrationExecutor(self.connection)
        executor.loader.replacements = {
            ("migrations", "0001_squashed_0002"): migrations.Migration(
                name="0001_squashed_0002",
                dependencies=[("migrations", "0001_initial"), ("migrations", "0002_second")],
                replaces=[("migrations", "0001_initial"), ("migrations", "0002_second")],
            ),
        }

        executor.check_replacements()

        self.assertIn(
            ("migrations", "0001_squashed_0002"),
            recorder.applied_migrations(),
        )

    def test_check_replacements_does_nothing_if_replaced_not_all_applied(self):
        """
        Tests that check_replacements does nothing if not all replaced
        migrations are applied.
        """
        recorder = MigrationRecorder(self.connection)
        recorder.record_applied("migrations", "0001_initial")

        executor = MigrationExecutor(self.connection)
        executor.loader.replacements = {
            ("migrations", "0001_squashed_0002"): migrations.Migration(
                name="0001_squashed_0002",
                dependencies=[("migrations", "0001_initial"), ("migrations", "0002_second")],

def test_latex_printer_mul_is_clean():
    x, y = symbols('x, y')
    f = Function('f')

    # Path 1: arg.is_Function is True
    assert not LatexPrinter._mul_is_clean(f(x) * y)

    # Path 2: arg.is_Function is False, loop continues, arg.is_Function is True
    assert not LatexPrinter._mul_is_clean(x * f(y))

    # Path 3: arg.is_Function is False, loop continues, arg.is_Function is False
    assert LatexPrinter._mul_is_clean(x * y)

    # Path 4: Loop doesn't execute
    assert LatexPrinter._mul_is_clean(x)

    # Path 5: Loop doesn't execute
    assert LatexPrinter._mul_is_clean(1)

    printer = LatexPrinter(settings)

    # Path 1: 'e' in str_real, exp[0] == '+', decimal_separator == 'comma'
    assert printer._print_Float(Float('1.0e100')) == r"1.0 \cdot 10^{100}"

    # Path 2: 'e' in str_real, exp[0] == '+', decimal_separator != 'comma'
    assert printer._print_Float(Float('1.0e-100')) == r"1.0 \cdot 10^{-100}"

    # Path 3: 'e' in str_real, exp[0] != '+', decimal_separator == 'comma'
    assert printer._print_Float(Float('-1.0e-100')) == r"- 1.0 \cdot 10^{-100}"

    # Path 4: 'e' in str_real, exp[0] != '+', decimal_separator != 'comma'
    assert printer._print_Float(Float('-1.0e100')) == r"- 1.0 \cdot 10^{100}"

    # Path 5: 'e' not in str_real, str_real == '+inf'
    assert printer._print_Float(Float('+inf')) == r"\infty"

    # Path 6: 'e' not in str_real, str_real == '-inf'
    assert printer._print_Float(Float('-inf')) == r"- \infty"

    # Path 7: 'e' not in str_real, str_real == '-inf', decimal_separator == 'comma'
    settings['decimal_separator'] = 'comma'
    assert printer._print_Float(Float('-1.234')) == r"- 1{,}234"

    # Path 8: 'e' not in str_real, str_real == '-inf', decimal_separator != 'comma'
    settings['decimal_separator'] = 'period'
    assert printer._print_Float(Float('-1.234')) == r"- 1.234"

from sympy import symbols, latex, S, Pow, Derivative
from sympy.printing.latex import LatexPrinter

x, y = symbols('x y')

def test_latex_printer_standard_power():
    # Path 1: expr.base.is_Symbol is True
    assert latex(Pow(x, 2)) == r"x^{2}"

    # Path 1: expr.base.is_Symbol is True, and base needs super parenthesization
    assert latex(Pow(x**2, 3)) == r"\left(x^{2}\right)^{3}"

    # Path 2: expr.base.is_Symbol is False, and base starts with \left( and is a derivative
    d = Derivative(x, y)
    assert latex(Pow(d, 2)) == r"\left(\frac{d}{d y} x\right)^{2}"

    # Path 2: expr.base.is_Symbol is False, and base starts with \left( and is a derivative, but doesn't match the pattern
    d = Derivative(x, y)
    assert latex(Pow(d, 3)) == r"\left(\frac{d}{d y} x\right)^{3}"

    # Path 3: expr.base.is_Symbol is False, and base doesn't start with \left(
    assert latex(Pow(x**2, 3)) == r"\left(x^{2}\right)^{3}"

def test_latex_function_printing():
    from sympy import sin, cos, tan, log, exp, Function, symbols, S
    from sympy.abc import x, y

    # Test cases for accepted functions
    assert latex(sin(x)) == r"\sin{\left(x \right)}"
    assert latex(cos(x)) == r"\cos{\left(x \right)}"
    assert latex(tan(x)) == r"\tan{\left(x \right)}"
    assert latex(log(x)) == r"\log{\left(x \right)}"
    assert latex(exp(x)) == r"e^{x}"

    # Test cases for custom functions
    f = Function('f')
    assert latex(f(x)) == r"f{\left(x \right)}"
    assert latex(f(x, y)) == r"f{\left(x, y \right)}"

    # Test cases for functions with exponents
    assert latex(sin(x)**2) == r"\sin^{2}{\left(x \right)}"
    assert latex(exp(x)**3) == r"e^{3 x}"

    # Test cases for functions with different inv_trig_style
    assert latex(sin(x), inv_trig_style='abbreviated') == r"\sin{\left(x \right)}"
    assert latex(sin(x), inv_trig_style='full') == r"\operatorname{sin}{\left(x \right)}"
    assert latex(sin(x), inv_trig_style='power') == r"\sin^{-1}{\left(x \right)}"

    # Test cases for functions with fold_func_brackets
    assert latex(sin(x), fold_func_brackets=True) == r"\sin {x}"
    assert latex(sin(2*x**2), fold_func_brackets=True) == r"\sin {2 x^{2}}"
    assert latex(sin(x**2), fold_func_brackets=True) == r"\sin {x^{2}}"

    # Test cases for functions that are not in accepted_latex_functions
    g = Function('g')
    assert latex(g(x)) == r"\operatorname{g}{\left(x \right)}"

    # Test cases for functions with complex arguments
    assert latex(sin(1+I)) == r"\sin{\left(1 + i \right)}"
    assert latex(cos(x*I)) == r"\cos{\left(i x \right)}"

    # Test cases for functions with S
    assert latex(sin(S.Pi)) == r"\sin{\left(\pi \right)}"
    assert latex(cos(S.Pi/2)) == r"\cos{\left(\frac{\pi}{2} \right)}"

def test_latex_Feedback():

    tf2 = TransferFunction(x - y, x + y, y)

    # and expr.den == tf
    assert LatexPrinter()._print_Feedback(tf1, tf2) == r'\left(\frac{x y^{2} - z}{- t^{3} + y^{3}}\right) \left(\frac{x - y}{x + y}\right)'

    # Path 2: isinstance(num, Series) and isinstance(expr.den, TransferFunction)
    # and expr.den == tf
    tf4 = TransferFunction(x, 1, x)
    assert LatexPrinter()._print_Feedback(tf1, tf4) == r'\left(\frac{x y^{2} - z}{- t^{3} + y^{3}}\right) \left(\frac{x}{x}\right)'

    # Path 3: isinstance(num, Series) and isinstance(expr.den, TransferFunction)
    # and expr.den != tf
    tf5 = TransferFunction(x + 1, 1, x)
    assert LatexPrinter()._print_Feedback(tf1, tf5) == r'\left(\frac{x y^{2} - z}{- t^{3} + y^{3}}\right) \left(\frac{x + 1}{1}\right)'

    # and num == tf
    tf6 = TransferFunction(x - 1, x + 1, x)
    assert LatexPrinter()._print_Feedback(tf6, tf1) == r'\left(\frac{x - 1}{x + 1}\right) \left(\frac{x y^{2} - z}{- t^{3} + y^{3}}\right)'

    # Path 5: isinstance(num, TransferFunction) and isinstance(expr.den, Series)
    # and num != tf
    tf7 = TransferFunction(x + 1, 2 - y, x)
    assert LatexPrinter()._print_Feedback(tf7, tf1) == r'\left(\frac{x + 1}{2 - y}\right) \left(\frac{x y^{2} - z}{- t^{3} + y^{3}}\right)'

    # Path 6: isinstance(num, TransferFunction) and isinstance(expr.den, Series)
    # and num == tf
    assert LatexPrinter()._print_Feedback(tf1, tf1) == r'\left(\frac{x y^{2} - z}{- t^{3} + y^{3}}\right) \left(\frac{x y^{2} - z}{- t^{3} + y^{3}}\right)'

    # Path 7: isinstance(num, TransferFunction) and isinstance(expr.den, Series)

    tf8 = TransferFunction(y, y**2 + 2*y + 3, y)

def test_StrPrinter_print_Rational():
    from sympy.printing.str import StrPrinter
    from sympy import Rational, S

    printer = StrPrinter()

    # Path 1: expr.q == 1
    assert printer._print_Rational(Rational(5)) == "5"
    assert printer._print_Rational(Rational(1)) == "1"
    assert printer._print_Rational(Rational(0)) == "0"

    # Path 2: expr.q != 1 and sympy_integers is True
    settings = {"sympy_integers": True}
    printer = StrPrinter(settings)
    assert printer._print_Rational(Rational(1, 2)) == "S(1)/2"
    assert printer._print_Rational(Rational(3, 4)) == "S(3)/4"
    assert printer._print_Rational(Rational(-1, 2)) == "S(-1)/2"

    # Path 3: expr.q != 1 and sympy_integers is False
    settings = {"sympy_integers": False}
    printer = StrPrinter(settings)
    assert printer._print_Rational(Rational(1, 2)) == "1/2"
    assert printer._print_Rational(Rational(3, 4)) == "3/4"
    assert printer._print_Rational(Rational(-1, 2)) == "-1/2"
    assert printer._print_Rational(Rational(2, 3)) == "2/3"
    assert printer._print_Rational(Rational(-2, 3)) == "-2/3"
    assert printer._print_Rational(Rational(0, 5)) == "0"
    assert printer._print_Rational(Rational(5, 0)) == "zoo"

        ],

    )
    code_gen = CCodeGen()
    code_lines = []
    dereference = []
    for arg in routine.arguments:
        if isinstance(arg, Equality) and not arg.dimensions:
            dereference.append(arg.lhs.name)
    return_val = None
    for result in routine.result_variables:
        if isinstance(result, Equality):
            assign_to = routine.name + '_result'
            t = result.lhs.get_datatype('C')
            code_lines.append('{0} {1};\n'.format(t, str(assign_to)))
            return_val = assign_to
        try:
            constants, not_c, c_expr = code_gen._printer_method_with_settings(
                'doprint',
                dict(human=False, dereference=dereference),
                result.rhs,
                assign_to=assign_to
            )
            for name, value in sorted(constants, key=str):
                code_lines.append('double const %s = %s;\n' % (name, value))
            code_lines.append('%s\n' % c_expr)
        except Exception as e:
            pass
    assert len(code_lines) > 0

            return func

        """
        class MockClass:
            pass
        
        obj = MockClass
        name = ""
        
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            method_decorator(lambda func: func)(obj)
        self.assertIn("name", str(context.exception))

    def test_method_decorator_dec_is_type_name_not_callable(self):
        """
        Test path 3: obj is a type, name exists, but attribute is not callable.
        """
        class MockClass:
            attribute = "not callable"
        
        obj = MockClass
        name = "attribute"
        
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError) as context:
            method_decorator(lambda func: func)(obj)
        self.assertIn("Cannot decorate", str(context.exception))

    def test_method_decorator_dec_is_type_name_is_callable(self):
        """

        name = "test_method"

from sympy import sin, Function, symbols, Dummy, Lambda, cos

from sympy.core.sympify import sympify
from sympy.abc import n, w, x, y, z
from sympy.testing.pytest import raises

def test_mathematica_parser_fullform_to_fullformsympy():
    parser = MathematicaParser()

    def converter(expr):
        if isinstance(expr, list):
            if len(expr) > 0:
                head = expr[0]
                args = [converter(arg) for arg in expr[1:]]
                return Function(head)(*args)
            else:
                raise ValueError("Empty list of expressions")
        elif isinstance(expr, str):
            return symbols(expr)
        else:
            return sympify(expr)

    # Test case for Path 1: List with elements
    assert converter(["Sin", ["Times", "x", "y"]]) == sin(x * y)
    assert converter(["Plus", ["Times", "x", "y"], "z"]) == x * y + z
    assert converter(["Sin", ["Times", "x", ["Plus", "y", "z"], ["Power", "w", "n"]]]) == sin(x * (y + z) * w**n)

    # Test case for Path 2: Empty list
    with raises(ValueError) as excinfo:
        converter([])
    assert str(excinfo.value) == "Empty list of expressions"

    # Test case for Path 3: String input
    assert converter("x") == x
    assert converter("y") == y
    assert converter("z") == z

    # Test case for Path 4: Non-string, non-list input
    assert converter(1) == 1
    assert converter(2.5) == 2.5

import sympy
from sympy.physics.units import Quantity, meter, second, kilogram, joule, dimension
from sympy.physics.units.systems import SI
from sympy.core.add import Add
from sympy.core.mul import Mul
from sympy.core.power import Pow
from sympy.functions.elementary.exponential import exp

def test_collect_factor_and_dimension_complex():
    u = Quantity("u")
    u.set_global_relative_scale_factor(1, meter)
    v = Quantity("v")
    v.set_global_relative_scale_factor(1, second)
    w = Quantity("w")
    w.set_global_relative_scale_factor(1, kilogram)

    # Path 1: Quantity
    factor1, dim1 = SI._collect_factor_and_dimension(u)
    assert factor1 == 1
    assert dim1 == meter

    # Path 2: Mul
    expr2 = u * v
    factor2, dim2 = SI._collect_factor_and_dimension(expr2)
    assert factor2 == 1
    assert dim2 == meter * second

    # Path 3: Pow
    expr3 = u**2
    factor3, dim3 = SI._collect_factor_and_dimension(expr3)
    assert factor3 == 1
    assert dim3 == meter**2

    # Path 4: Add
    expr4 = u + v
    factor4, dim4 = SI._collect_factor_and_dimension(expr4)
    assert factor4 == 1
    assert dim4 == meter

    # Path 5: Mul and Pow
    expr5 = (u * v)**2
    factor5, dim5 = SI._collect_factor_and_dimension(expr5)
    assert factor5 == 1
    assert dim5 == (meter * second)**2

    # Path 6: Add and Mul
    expr6 = u + u * v
    factor6, dim6 = SI._collect_factor_and_dimension(expr6)
    assert factor6 == 1
    assert dim6 == meter

    # Path 7: Add with incompatible dimensions
    expr7 = u + w
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        SI._collect_factor_and_dimension(expr7)

    # Path 8: Complex expression
    expr8 = (u * v)**2 + w
    factor8, dim8 = SI._collect_factor_and_dimension(expr8)
    assert factor8 == 1
    assert dim8 == (meter * second)**2 * kilogram

    # Path 9: Expression with exp
    expr9 = exp(u)
    factor9, dim9 = SI._collect_factor_and_dimension(expr9)
    assert factor9 == sympy.E
    assert dim9 == Dimension(1)

    # Path 10: Expression with exp and mul
    expr10 = exp(u * v)
    factor10, dim10 = SI._collect_factor_and_dimension(expr10)
    assert factor10 == sympy.E
    assert dim10 == Dimension(1)

from django.core.management import BaseCommand, CommandError

def test_basecommand_init_no_color_force_color():
    with pytest.raises(CommandError) as excinfo:
        BaseCommand(no_color=True, force_color=True)
    assert str(excinfo.value) == "'no_color' and 'force_color' can't be used together."

def test_basecommand_init_no_color():
    cmd = BaseCommand(no_color=True)
    assert cmd.style is BaseCommand.no_style()
    assert cmd.stderr.style_func is None

def test_basecommand_init_force_color():
    cmd = BaseCommand(force_color=True)
    assert cmd.style is BaseCommand.color_style(force_color=True)
    assert cmd.stderr.style_func is BaseCommand.color_style(force_color=True).ERROR

def test_basecommand_init_invalid_requires_system_checks():
    with pytest.raises(TypeError) as excinfo:
        BaseCommand(requires_system_checks="invalid")
    assert str(excinfo.value) == "requires_system_checks must be a list or tuple."

def test_basecommand_init_default_values():
    cmd = BaseCommand()
    assert cmd.stdout.isatty()
    assert cmd.stderr.isatty()
    assert cmd.style is BaseCommand.color_style()
    assert cmd.stderr.style_func is BaseCommand.color_style().ERROR

import unittest
from argparse import ArgumentParser

from django.core.management import BaseCommand

class TestBaseCommandAddBaseArgument(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_add_base_argument_suppress_help(self):
        base_command = BaseCommand()
        base_command.suppressed_base_arguments = {"--version"}
        parser = ArgumentParser()
        base_command.add_base_argument(parser, "--version", action="version", version="1.0")
        self.assertIn("--version", parser.format_help())

        base_command.suppressed_base_arguments = {"--verbosity"}
        parser = ArgumentParser()
        base_command.add_base_argument(parser, "-v", "--verbosity", action="store", default=1)
        self.assertNotIn("--verbosity", parser.format_help())

    def test_add_base_argument_no_suppression(self):
        base_command = BaseCommand()
        parser = ArgumentParser()
        base_command.add_base_argument(parser, "--foo", help="Foo help")
        self.assertIn("--foo", parser.format_help())

    def test_add_base_argument_multiple_args(self):
        base_command = BaseCommand()
        base_command.suppressed_base_arguments = {"--version"}
        parser = ArgumentParser()
        base_command.add_base_argument(parser, "--version", action="version", version="1.0")
        base_command.add_base_argument(parser, "--foo", help="Foo help")
        self.assertIn("--version", parser.format_help())
        self.assertIn("--foo", parser.format_help())

    def test_add_base_argument_with_kwargs(self):
        base_command = BaseCommand()
        parser = ArgumentParser()
        base_command.add_base_argument(parser, "--bar", help="Bar help", default="default_bar")
        self.assertIn("--bar", parser.format_help())
        self.assertEqual(parser.get_default("bar"), "default_bar")

from django.test import TestCase
from django.core.checks import Tags
from django.core.management import BaseCommand
from django.apps import apps

class BaseCommandCheckTests(TestCase):
    def test_check_with_no_issues(self):
        """Test that check() returns without raising an error when there are no issues."""
        # Mock the check framework to avoid actual checks
        mock_check = self.mock_check()
        BaseCommand.check = mock_check

        # Call check with some dummy arguments
        BaseCommand.check(tags=[Tags.models], display_num_errors=False)

        # Assert that the mock check was called
        self.assertTrue(mock_check.called)

    def test_check_with_serious_issues(self):
        """Test that check() raises SystemCheckError when serious issues are found."""
        # Mock the check framework to raise SystemCheckError
        mock_check = self.mock_check(raise_error=True)
        BaseCommand.check = mock_check

        # Call check with some dummy arguments
        with self.assertRaises(SystemCheckError):
            BaseCommand.check(tags=[Tags.models], display_num_errors=False)

        # Assert that the mock check was called
        self.assertTrue(mock_check.called)

    def test_check_with_non_serious_issues(self):
        """Test that check() doesn't raise an error when non-serious issues are found."""
        # Mock the check framework to return non-serious issues
        mock_check = self.mock_check(return_issues=[{'level': 'WARNING'}])
        BaseCommand.check = mock_check

        # Call check with some dummy arguments
        BaseCommand.check(tags=[Tags.models], display_num_errors=False)

        # Assert that the mock check was called
        self.assertTrue(mock_check.called)

    def mock_check(self, raise_error=False, return_issues=None):
        """Helper function to mock the BaseCommand.check method."""
        mock = self.mock_open()
        mock.called = False
        if raise_error:
            def check(*args, **kwargs):
                mock.called = True
                raise SystemCheckError("Mock SystemCheckError")
            return check
        else:
            def check(*args, **kwargs):
                mock.called = True
                if return_issues:
                    return return_issues
            return check

        @pytest.mark.asyncio

        """
    )

        @pytest.mark.asyncio
        async def test_async_function():

        """
    )

    pytester = Pytester(

                    pass

def test_path_matches_patterns_covers_all_paths():
    config = Config(workdir=".")
    patterns = ["test_*.py", "*_test.py"]

    # Path 1: name.startswith(option) is True
    assert _pytest.pathlib.path_matches_patterns(Path("test_abc.py"), patterns) == True

    # Path 2: name.startswith(option) is False, and fnmatch is True
    assert _pytest.pathlib.path_matches_patterns(Path("abc_test.py"), patterns) == True

    # Path 3: name.startswith(option) is False, fnmatch is False, and there are more options
    assert _pytest.pathlib.path_matches_patterns(Path("other_file.py"), patterns) == False

    # Path 4: name.startswith(option) is False, fnmatch is False, and there are more options
    assert _pytest.pathlib.path_matches_patterns(Path("abc_test.py"), ["test_*.py"]) == False

    # Path 5: name.startswith(option) is False, fnmatch is False, and there are more options
    assert _pytest.pathlib.path_matches_patterns(Path("test_abc.py"), ["*_test.py"]) == False

    # Path 6: name.startswith(option) is False, fnmatch is False, and there are no more options
    assert _pytest.pathlib.path_matches_patterns(Path("other_file.py"), ["test_*.py", "*_test.py"]) == False

    # Path 7: No options
    assert _pytest.pathlib.path_matches_patterns(Path("other_file.py"), []) == False

def test_setmulti2_duplicate_arg(pytester: Pytester) -> None:
    """Test that setmulti2 raises ValueError when an argument is duplicated."""
    callspec = pytest.CallSpec2(None)
    argnames = ["arg1", "arg2"]
    valset = [1, 2]
    valtypes = {"arg1": "params", "arg2": "funcargs"}

    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as excinfo:
        callspec.setmulti2(valtypes, argnames, valset, "id", [], 0, 0)
    assert "duplicate arg1" in str(excinfo.value)


def test_setmulti2_params_and_funcargs(pytester: Pytester) -> None:
    """Test that setmulti2 correctly sets params and funcargs."""
    callspec = pytest.CallSpec2(None)
    argnames = ["arg1", "arg2"]
    valset = [1, "hello"]
    valtypes = {"arg1": "params", "arg2": "funcargs"}

    callspec.setmulti2(valtypes, argnames, valset, "id", [], 0, 0)

    assert "arg1" in callspec.params
    assert callspec.params["arg1"] == 1
    assert "arg2" in callspec.funcargs
    assert callspec.funcargs["arg2"] == "hello"
    assert callspec.indices["arg1"] == 0
    assert callspec.indices["arg2"] == 1
    assert callspec.keywords == {}


def test_setmulti2_multiple_iterations(pytester: Pytester) -> None:
    """Test that setmulti2 correctly handles multiple iterations."""
    callspec = pytest.CallSpec2(None)
    argnames = ["arg1", "arg2"]
    valset1 = [1, "hello"]
    valset2 = [2, "world"]
    valtypes = {"arg1": "params", "arg2": "funcargs"}

    callspec.setmulti2(valtypes, argnames, valset1, "id1", [], 0, 0)
    callspec.setmulti2(valtypes, argnames, valset2, "id2", [], 1, 1)

    assert "arg1" in callspec.params
    assert callspec.params["arg1"] == 1
    assert "arg2" in callspec.funcargs
    assert callspec.funcargs["arg2"] == "hello"
    assert "arg1" in callspec.params
    assert callspec.params["arg1"] == 2
    assert "arg2" in callspec.funcargs
    assert callspec.funcargs["arg2"] == "world"
    assert len(callspec._idlist) == 2
    assert callspec._idlist == ["id1", "id2"]
